anchors.paper_title: Movement‐induced hypoalgesia: behavioral characteristics and neural mechanisms
anchors.paper_venue: Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences
anchors.reason: The paper discusses movement-induced hypoalgesia and neural mechanisms, which is topically related to the dataset's pain assessment task, but does not describe or introduce this specific dataset.

metadata.methods_description: Laser stimuli of varying intensities were administered to participants. Individual pain thresholds were determined by identifying the energy intensity corresponding to an average pain rating of 7. Each participant received 10 laser stimulations and rated pain intensity and unpleasantness on a numeric rating scale (0-10) via mouse-click responses on a screen. Participants were instructed to maintain visual fixation on a crosshair, with 5-second intervals between stimulation and rating, and randomized inter-trial intervals of 5 seconds following pain ratings.

citation_details.author: Zhao Xiangyue, Zhou Jingyao, 张丽波 ZHANG Libo, Duan Haoqing, Wei Shiyu, Bi Yanzhi, Hu Li
citation_details.abstract: This dataset comprises neurophysiological recordings from 39 participants who received calibrated laser stimuli while rating pain intensity and unpleasantness. Participants were presented with laser stimulations at individually-determined energy levels and provided subjective pain ratings on a 0-10 numeric rating scale. The study investigates the neural mechanisms underlying pain perception and assessment, with potential applications to understanding movement-induced hypoalgesia and related pain modulation phenomena. This is a derivative dataset based on OpenNeuro ds005289.
